# Third-party licences: Rust crates

Generated by `node scripts/third-party-licenses/generate.js` from `src-tauri/Cargo.lock`, the crate sources in the Cargo registry and the Rust toolchain. Do not edit by hand: run the command again after any change to `Cargo.lock` and with each new toolchain the release builds use.

Scope: the Rust standard library and every crate in `src-tauri/Cargo.lock` except AstroBurst itself, 705 crates. 409 of the crates are linked into a release build of the desktop app. "Linked into" names the release builds whose `astroburst` binary links the crate with the default features (`cargo tree -e normal,no-proc-macro --target <triple>` for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin; macOS is the universal build of the two Apple targets). "compile time" marks procedural macros and the crates only they use: they run during the build and are not linked. "no" marks build-script, test-only, headless-server-only and other-platform crates; they are listed so that the list covers the whole lock file.

Rust standard library: the first entry. Every release build links `std`, `core` and `alloc` into the `astroburst` binary, but they come with the Rust toolchain, not from `Cargo.lock`. The entry's version is the `rustc` release this list was generated with (`rustc -vV` in `src-tauri`). `.github/workflows/release.yml` installs the toolchain of the release builds with `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.96.0`, that release exactly, and the generator stops when the `rustc` it runs is another release. The copyright cell and texts follow the toolchain's own `share/doc/rust/COPYRIGHT-library.html`: the library's licence, the in-tree files under other terms, and the out-of-tree crates built into the library for any target, with the licence texts it reproduces and, for the library's own licences, the texts in the toolchain's `share/doc/rust/licenses` folder.

Licence texts: each entry names the texts the crate ships: files named LICENSE, LICENCE, COPYING, COPYRIGHT, NOTICE, PATENTS or UNLICENSE at the crate root or in its source folders (tests, benches and examples excluded), any `LICENSES` folder and the manifest's `license-file`. alloc-stdlib also names `alloc-stdlib-LICENSE` from this folder (the LICENSE of its repository, which the crate does not ship); webview2-com-sys also names `webview2-loader-LICENSE.txt` from this folder (for WebView2LoaderStatic.lib, which the Windows build links statically); `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` explains these files. Where a crate ships no licence text (none, or only an SPDX metadata file) and no file of this folder stands in for it, the entry adds the SPDX standard text of the licence taken from its expression (MIT where the expression offers it). The copyright column repeats the copyright lines of those files; where they have none it gives the authors from the manifest. Texts that differ only in white space are printed once under Texts, as their first user ships them.
